prompt:
Our VCF 9.1 application rollout creates an NSX group and then a distributed-firewall security policy. Build a PowerShell module that performs those two NSX Policy writes in order and never repeats a completed group write when the later policy write fails.

Before implementing, research the `PatchGroupForDomain` and `PatchSecurityPolicyForDomain` operations and the corresponding VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 generated model types in official VMware sources. Confirm their paths, methods, request and response shapes, and authentication behavior, and cite the source URLs consulted.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed. In particular, `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` and its official `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency load the generated `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.*` types. Do not install, copy, generate, or vendor any VMware module, assembly, SDK, or OpenAPI specification. Your module manifest must declare `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` as a required module, and the model builders below must return the real generated NSX binding types from that prerequisite.

Create `VcfNsxPolicy/VcfNsxPolicy.psd1` and `VcfNsxPolicy/VcfNsxPolicy.psm1`, exporting exactly these functions:

- `New-VcfNsxGroupModel -DisplayName <string> -TagValue <string> [-Description <string>]` returns a `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.Group`. It contains one `Condition` expression with `resource_type=Condition`, `member_type=VirtualMachine`, `key=Tag`, `operator=EQUALS`, and the supplied value.
- `New-VcfNsxSecurityPolicyModel -DisplayName <string> -SourceGroupPath <string> -DestinationGroupPath <string> [-SequenceNumber <uint32>] [-Description <string>] [-RuleNotes <string>]` returns a `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.SecurityPolicy`. It is an Application, stateful policy with one ALLOW, IN_OUT rule named `allow-<source group id>-to-<destination group id>`, scoped to ANY and using service ANY. The default sequence number is 1200.
- `Invoke-VcfNsxPolicyRollout -BaseUri <uri> -DomainId <string> -GroupId <string> -TagValue <string> -SecurityPolicyId <string> -DestinationGroupId <string> -Username <string> -Password <string> [-SequenceNumber <uint32>] [-Description <string>] [-RuleNotes <string>]` creates the two typed models, serializes them with their generated `ToJson()` methods, and invokes `PatchGroupForDomain` followed by `PatchSecurityPolicyForDomain`, exactly once each. `BaseUri` is the NSX manager origin; append the documented `/policy/api/v1` base path. Escape each path ID as one URI segment. Send `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and HTTP Basic authentication using the supplied username and password.

Accept only each operation's documented 200 response as success. If the policy PATCH fails after the group PATCH succeeds, report the policy failure without replaying the group request. Return an object with `GroupId`, `SecurityPolicyId`, and `CompletedOperations` in completion order after both writes succeed.

When `Description` and `RuleNotes` are not supplied, do not substitute empty strings, empty arrays, false, zero, or null. Leave the generated properties unset so `ToJson()` omits them.

Edit only the files under `VcfNsxPolicy/`. Run `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File test_nsx_policy.ps1`.
notes: VCF 9.1 NSX Policy integration exercise covering generated VMware binding models, exact PATCH requests, Basic authentication, optional-property omission, and ordered partial work.
